newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Friday:

Spokesman Klaus van der Pas denied newspaper reports that "Brussels bureaucrats" planned a scheme to erect statues of EU luminaries such as Jacques Delors and Jacques Santer across Europe. He said the reports were based on a resolution by the European Parliament on setting aside money in public works contracts for works of art, which did not mention statues.
Spokesman Jochen Kubosch said the informal industry council in The Hague would focus on the EU's industrial competitiveness.

In response to a question about ethnic diversity in EU institutions, spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said the recruitment policy was based on non-discrimination and that announcements of "concours" would henceforth include a specific reference to that policy. He said the Commission did not, however, plan to keep a count of civil servants' ethnic origins.

Spokesman Josep Coll i Corbo said the Commission was not involved in a meeting between Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok in The Hague. He said Arafat planned to attend the February 24 General Affairs Council to sign a cooperation agreement with the EU and could meet with the Commission then.
Spokesmen Jochen Kubosch and Betty Olivi said Commissioners Martin Bangemann and Mario Monti had not been involved in the Spanish digital TV controversy.
Spokesman Patrick Child said Eurostat would announce decisions on Monday that would address certain aspects of Italy's EMU-related budget policy.

Spokesman Costas Verros said the Commission was discussing whether to revise its policy against selling airport slots, but that had no link to decisions about the British Airways/American Airlines or other alliances.

- Speech/97/26: Speech by Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan at the World Economic Forum, "Globalisation: Responding to new political and moral challenges".
- Eurostat: Statistics in Focus - Population and social conditions 1997/1 - The economic activity of women in the European Union.
